column1: # Which version file owns which consumer. scripts/toolchain-drift-check.sh reads
# this table and nothing else to decide where an Erlang/Elixir version may live.
# Columns: <owner> <consumer>, whitespace-separated, one consumer a row. The
#   .github/workflows/X.yml       every erlef/setup-beam step in X reads the file
#   .github/workflows/X.yml#job   the same, for one job; beats the workflow row
#   .github/actions/X/action.yml  the same, for a composite action
#   */Dockerfile, *.sh, ...       a literal version in it (an image tag, an
#                                 install default) must equal the file's, or it
#   *.tool-versions               that file's erlang line equals this file's
#   data <file>                   its literals are test data or past check names,
#                                 not a runtime; an install, image or *_VERSION
# Every tracked .tool-versions / *.tool-versions must appear here. A literal
# version in a workflow, action, Dockerfile, deploy file or script with no row
# fails. Moving a consumer to another file is editing its row; folding a
# version file into another is deleting its rows and re-pointing its consumers.
# The content server's runtime: asdf on the box resolves the repo-root file.
# The release images: the control plane builds cloud/Dockerfile, and
# The formatter the format gate measures (reason in the file).
# Test data: fake toolchains, and the names of past CI checks
